symptoms: Yellow patches along leaf veins, brown streaks on green stems, and brown dry rot inside the roots. Roots can look fine outside but be spoiled inside.
cause: Cassava brown streak viruses, spread by whiteflies and by planting infected cuttings.
cultural_control: Plant only clean cuttings from healthy plants. Uproot and destroy infected plants early. Harvest sooner in affected fields. Do not move cuttings from infected gardens.
chemical_option: No chemical cures the virus. Controlling whiteflies with sprays is not reliable.
prevention: Use tolerant or resistant varieties recommended locally. Ask NARO or your extension officer for current recommended varieties and certified clean planting material.
see_officer_when: Many plants in the field show symptoms, or you want certified clean planting material.
source: Draft knowledge entry to verify against NARO, MAAIF, and FAO guidance.
